what_happened: While the stated focus was "make Athena faster first", the median time per landed job rose from about 25 to about 60 minutes between 29 Oct and 4 Nov. Nobody noticed during that week. The person running Athena queued quality steps (planning for more jobs, proof runs) without weighing the time they added. The throughput review's own speed design request sat queued for 6 days. The person running Athena had tracked GitHub test-run time as the speed measure, not whole-job time, so the measure did not show the slowdown. This was not a job rejection and no checks or criteria failed. It was a design mistake found afterwards.
cause: Athena has no standing measure of the thing the current focus names. Whole-job time per landed job is never computed, trended or compared with a baseline. New steps are queued with no recorded time cost, and the work that serves the focus is ranked like any other queue item. Detection depends on a person noticing, as with code health. The person running Athena chose a convenient proxy (CI test time) because nothing supplied the real measure.
prevention: A standing check, run on each drain, that computes median whole-job time (start to landed) over a rolling window from the job records. It compares that median with the baseline recorded when the focus was set. When it exceeds a set threshold (for example 25% worse), it queues an urgent review and shows the figures with the drain summary. A request that adds a stage or proof run must also state its expected time cost. When the focus is speed, the work that serves that focus is ranked ahead of other work.
proposed_request: Add a throughput watch to Athena. On each drain, compute from the job records the median time from job start to landed, for landed jobs in the last 7 days. Also compute the median for the 7 days before that. Show both numbers in the drain summary. When the recent median is more than 25% above the earlier one, queue an urgent item titled "job time has risen" with both figures, the per-stage breakdown (planning, producer, verifier, checks, landing) and the stage that grew most. Record the baseline when a focus is set on speed. Acceptance: (1) a test with fixture job records shows the numbers and the queued item when the rise is over 25%; (2) a test shows no item when the rise is under 25%; (3) a test shows the absent-data case (fewer than 3 landed jobs in a window) reports "not enough data" and queues nothing; (4) the summary is printed on a real drain against existing records.
